chapter: Charleston childhood and the Jenkins Orphanage
title: His father's job and parents born into slavery
summary: Briggs describes his father's position in the Sanitary Department and good education, and says his parents were born slaves but never spoke of it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: 'Cause through the churches, our parents had enough money to pay --
Well, your Dad had a pretty good job down there, for a black --
Yes, very good. He was a sanitary inspector. He was not what you would call a principal sanitary. He was under, you know, control.
He had a position in the Sanitary Department.
But he wasn't working day labor like most of the blacks down there?
No, no, no, not scavenger work.
No, he had a more or
I couldn't say what type of job he had, but I think he was a -- he had a pretty good education.
Yes, I think the people who were taking care of his parents, grandparents, you know, they were pretty good to him and his family.
I see. Well, I have just again to go back a little bit, he was actually -- he and your Mom were actually born as slaves?
So they could have remembered even another time?
Yes. As far as they were concerned, Dad never spoke to us about what happened.
